description.value: Mount Robson Park protects the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies (3,954 m) and is one of British Columbia's most celebrated provincial parks. The 63 km Mount Robson Corridor follows Highway 16 (Yellowhead), giving touring cyclists dramatic views of mountains, creeks, and wetlands as they pass through. A Welcome Centre at the park's western entrance serves as an orientation point, and the world-renowned Berg Lake Trail draws backcountry adventurers from around the globe.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content from bcparks.ca/mount-robson-park/ confirms an active, major provincial park along Highway 16 in the Canadian Rockies, with a Welcome Centre at the western entrance and campgrounds along the corridor. No specific bike parking, washroom facilities, or water refill points are named on the park webpage — the corridor is described as having 'facilities' but with no itemized detail — so all amenity fields remain null. The BC Parks general contact number (1-800-689-9025) is drawn from the contact subpage; OSM carries no phone or address, so contact_confirmed reflects this asymmetry.
concerns: OSM record is a single node with minimal tags (no address, phone, or amenity data); the park covers a large area and a single point may not adequately represent it.
Phone listed (1-800-689-9025) is the general BC Parks contact centre, not a park-specific line.
Restaurant, gift store, and gas station are described as 'nearby' the western entrance — not confirmed as within the park boundary, so on-site food remains unverified.
OSM community field lists 'Unknown / Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior' but the BC Parks page places the park in the Omineca region.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Mount Robson Park is one of BC's most iconic destinations and sits directly on Highway 16 (Yellowhead), a major touring corridor; it offers clear value to touring cyclists and warrants a directory listing.

wow_evidence: Highest peak in the Canadian Rockies (3,954 m), internationally known; the Highway 16 corridor view of Robson is a trip-defining moment for Yellowhead riders (Emerald-class anchor).
blurb: Home of Mount Robson, the Canadian Rockies' highest peak; the Yellowhead runs beneath it.
